text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\sec y\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}+2x\sin y=x^{3}\cos y,y(1)=0$. Then $y(\sqrt{3})$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \sec y\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2x\sin y=x^{3}\cos y \\ \Rightarrow \sec ^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2x\tan y=x^{3} \end{array}$

Let $z=\tan y$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{dz}{dx}=\sec ^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{dz}{dx}+2xz=x^{3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{I.F.}=e^{x^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow z.e^{x^{2}}=\int e^{x^{2}}\cdot x^{3}dx+c \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow \tan y\cdot e^{x^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\left (x^{2}e^{x^{2}}-e^{x^{2}}\right )+c$

$\Rightarrow \tan (0)\cdot e=\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot e-e)+c$

$\Rightarrow c=0$

$\Rightarrow \tan y=\frac{x^{2}-1}{2}$

$y=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )\Rightarrow y(\sqrt{3})=\frac{π}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: There are three bags $X,Y$ and $Z$. Bag $X$ contains 5 one-rupee coins and 4 five-rupee coins; Bag $Y$ contains 4 one-rupee coins and 5 five-rupee coins and Bag $Z$ contains 3 one-rupee coins and 6 five-rupee coins. A bag is selected at random and a coin drawn from it at random is found to be a one-rupee coin. Then the probability, that it came from bag $\mathrm{Y}$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we use Bayes' theorem. Let's define the events:

$X$: Selecting bag $X$

$Y$: Selecting bag $Y$

$Z$: Selecting bag $Z$

$A$: Drawing a one-rupee coin

We are given that a bag is selected at random, so the probabilities for choosing any of the bags are:

$P(X)=P(Y)=P(Z)=\frac{1}{3}$

Next, we need the probability of drawing a one-rupee coin from each bag:

From bag $X$: $P(A|X)=\frac{5}{5+4}=\frac{5}{9}$

From bag $Y$: $P(A|Y)=\frac{4}{4+5}=\frac{4}{9}$

From bag $Z$: $P(A|Z)=\frac{3}{3+6}=\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}$

We need to find the probability that the coin came from bag $Y$ given that a one-rupee coin was drawn, i.e., we need $P(Y|A)$. Using Bayes' theorem:

$P(Y|A)=\frac{P(A|Y)\cdot P(Y)}{P(A)}$

To find $P(A)$, the total probability of drawing a one-rupee coin can be calculated as follows:

$P(A)=P(A|X)\cdot P(X)+P(A|Y)\cdot P(Y)+P(A|Z)\cdot P(Z)$

Substituting the values:

$P(A)=\left (\frac{5}{9}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\right )+\left (\frac{4}{9}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\right )$

Calculating the above, we get:

$P(A)=\frac{5}{27}+\frac{4}{27}+\frac{1}{9}$

Note that $\frac{1}{9}=\frac{3}{27}$, so:

$P(A)=\frac{5}{27}+\frac{4}{27}+\frac{3}{27}=\frac{12}{27}=\frac{4}{9}$

Now, substituting back into Bayes' theorem:

$P(Y|A)=\frac{\left (\frac{4}{9}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{3}\right )}{\frac{4}{9}}=\frac{4}{9}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{9}{4}=\frac{1}{3}$

Hence, the probability that the coin came from bag $Y$ is:

Option B: $\frac{1}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: If the line segment joining the points $(5,2)$ and $(2,a)$ subtends an angle $\frac{π}{4}$ at the origin, then the absolute value of the product of all possible values of $a$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we will use the concept of the slope and tangent of the angle subtended by the line segments at the origin.

Given points: $(5,2)$ and $(2,a)$

The slope of the line joining the origin and $(5,2)$ is:

$m_{1}=\frac{2-0}{5-0}=\frac{2}{5}$

The slope of the line joining the origin and $(2,a)$ is:

$m_{2}=\frac{a-0}{2-0}=\frac{a}{2}$

The line segment joining these points subtends an angle $θ=\frac{π}{4}$ at the origin.

According to the tangent formula for the angle between two lines:

$\tan θ=\left |\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{1+m_{1}m_{2}}\right |$

Here, $θ=\frac{π}{4}$ so, $\tan \left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=1$. Therefore,

$1=\left |\frac{\frac{a}{2}-\frac{2}{5}}{1+\left (\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{a}{2}\right )}\right |$

This simplifies to:

$1=\left |\frac{\frac{5a-4}{10}}{1+\frac{2a}{10}}\right |$

Multiplying both the numerator and denominator by 10 to simplify:

$1=\left |\frac{5a-4}{10+2a}\right |$

This leads to two equations due to the absolute value:

1. $5a-4=10+2a$

$3a=14$

$a=\frac{14}{3}$

2. $5a-4=-(10+2a)$

$5a-4=-10-2a$

$7a=-6$

$a=-\frac{6}{7}$

Thus, the possible values of $a$ are $\frac{14}{3}$ and $-\frac{6}{7}$.

The product of these values is:

$\left |\frac{14}{3}\times -\frac{6}{7}\right |$

$=\left |-\frac{84}{21}\right |$

$=|-4|$

$=4$

Therefore, the absolute value of the product of all possible values of $a$ is 4.

Answer: Option A
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: Let $\int\limits _{α}^{\log _{e}4}\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}^{x}-1}}=\frac{π}{6}$. Then $\mathrm{e}^{α}$ and $\mathrm{e}^{-α}$ are the roots of the equation :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Let}\sqrt{e^{x}-1}=t \\ e^{x}-1=t^{2} \\ e^{x}=1+t^{2} \\ e^{x}=0+2t\dfrac{dt}{dx} \\ \dfrac{dt}{dx}=\dfrac{e^{x}}{2t}=\dfrac{t^{2}+1}{2t} \\ I=\int \dfrac{2t}{t(1+t^{2})}dt=2\tan ^{-1}t \\ \Rightarrow I=\int\limits _{α}^{\log 4}\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{e^{x}-1}} \\ I=2\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{e^{x}-1}\left |_{α}^{\log 4} \\ =2\left (\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{3}-\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{e^{α}-1}\right )=\dfrac{π}{6} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{π}{3}-\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{e^{α}-1}\right )=\dfrac{π}{12} \\ \tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{e^{α}-1}\right )=\dfrac{π}{4} \\ \Rightarrow e^{α}-1=1 \\ e^{α}=2\Rightarrow e^{-α}=\dfrac{1}{2} \end{array} \right.$

$\begin{array}{lllllll} |A|=18-μ-4(14-5μ)-1(7-45)=0 \\ \Rightarrow 18-μ-56+20μ+38=0 \\ \Rightarrow 19μ=0 \\ \Rightarrow μ=0 \\ \text{Also adjA}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 18 & -9 & 9 \\ -14 & 7 & -7 \\ -38 & 19 & -19 \end{array}\right ] \\ (\text{adj}A)\cdot B=0 \\ \left [\begin{array}{lll} 18 & -9 & 9 \\ -14 & 7 & -7 \\ -38 & 19 & -19 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} λ \\ -3 \\ -1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ] \\ 18λ+27-9=0 \\ \Rightarrow 18λ=-18 \\ \Rightarrow λ=-1 \\ \Rightarrow 2μ+3λ=3(-1)=-3 \end{array}$

text: In an increasing geometric progression of positive terms, the sum of the second and sixth terms is $\frac{70}{3}$ and the product of the third and fifth terms is 49. Then the sum of the $4^{\text{th}},6^{\text{th}}$ and $8^{\text{th}}$ terms is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's denote the first term of the geometric progression by $a$ and the common ratio by $r$. The terms of the geometric progression can be written as follows:

First term: $a$

Second term: $ar$

Third term: $(ar^{2})$

Fourth term: $(ar^{3})$

Fifth term: $(ar^{4})$

Sixth term: $(ar^{5})$

Eighth term: $(ar^{7})$

We are given two key pieces of information:

1. The sum of the second and sixth terms is $\frac{70}{3}$:

$ar+ar^{5}=\frac{70}{3}$

2. The product of the third and fifth terms is 49:

$(ar^{2})\cdot (ar^{4})=49$

$a^{2}r^{6}=49$

$a^{2}=\frac{49}{r^{6}}$

$a=\frac{7}{r^{3}}$

Substituting $a=\frac{7}{r^{3}}$ into the first equation:

$\frac{7}{r^{3}}\cdot r+\frac{7}{r^{3}}\cdot r^{5}=\frac{70}{3}$

$\frac{7r}{r^{3}}+\frac{7r^{5}}{r^{3}}=\frac{70}{3}$

$\frac{7}{r^{2}}+\frac{7r^{2}}{1}=\frac{70}{3}$

Let $x=r^{2}$. Then:

$\frac{7}{x}+7x=\frac{70}{3}$

Multiply through by 3x to clear the denominator:

$21+21x^{2}=70x$

Rearrange into a standard quadratic equation:

$21x^{2}-70x+21=0$

Divide by 7 to simplify:

$3x^{2}-10x+3=0$

Solve this quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:

$x=\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$

Where $a=3$, $b=-10$, and $c=3$. Thus:

$x=\frac{10\pm \sqrt{100-36}}{6}$

$x=\frac{10\pm \sqrt{64}}{6}$

$x=\frac{10\pm 8}{6}$

$x=3$ or $x=\frac{1}{3}$

Since $x=r^{2}$ and $r$ is positive, we get $r=\sqrt{3}$ or $r=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. We need to choose the value that results in positive, increasing terms:

If $r=\sqrt{3}$:

$a=\frac{7}{r^{3}}=\frac{7}{(\sqrt{3})^{3}}=\frac{7}{3\sqrt{3}}=\frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{9}$

Now we can determine the sum of the 4th, 6th, and 8th terms:

The 4th term is: $ar^{3}=\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{9}\cdot 3\sqrt{3}=7$

The 6th term is: $ar^{5}=\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{9}\cdot 9\sqrt{3}=21$

The 8th term is: $ar^{7}=\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{9}\cdot 27(\sqrt{3})=63$

Adding these together:

$(4th+6th+8thterms)=7+21+63=91$

Therefore, the sum of the 4th, 6th, and 8th terms is 91.

Correct answer:

Option C: 91
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

$\frac{1}{\sqrt{29+(λ-5)^{2}}}[5+4+3(λ-5)]=3$

Squaring both sides

text: The sum of all possible values of $θ\in [-π,2π]$, for which $\frac{1+i\cos θ}{1-2i\cos θ}$ is purely imaginary, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{1+i\cos θ}{1-2i\cos θ}$ is purely imaginary

$n=\frac{1+i\cos θ}{1-2i\cos θ}\times \frac{1+2i\cos θ}{1+2i\cos θ}=\frac{1+3i\cos θ-2\cos ^{2}θ}{1+4\cos ^{2}θ}$

$n=\frac{1-2\cos ^{2}θ}{1+4\cos ^{2}θ}+i\left (\frac{3\cos θ}{1+4\cos ^{2}θ}\right )$

$n$ is purely imaginary

$\Rightarrow \frac{1-2\cos ^{2}θ}{1+4\cos ^{2}θ}=0$

$\Rightarrow \cos ^{2}θ=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \cos θ=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$θ$ can be $\frac{π}{4},\frac{-π}{4},\frac{3π}{4},\frac{-3π}{4},\frac{5π}{4},\frac{7π}{4}$

Sum of all possible values of $θ=3π$

text: If the value of $\frac{3\cos 36^{\circ }+5\sin 18^{\circ }}{5\cos 36^{\circ }-3\sin 18^{\circ }}$ is $\frac{a\sqrt{5}-b}{c}$, where $a,b,c$ are natural numbers and $\gcd (a,c)=1$, then $a+b+c$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the value of $\frac{3\cos 36^{\circ }+5\sin 18^{\circ }}{5\cos 36^{\circ }-3\sin 18^{\circ }}$ in the form $\frac{a\sqrt{5}-b}{c}$, we need to simplify the given expression. Let's start by using some fundamental trigonometric identities.

We know that:

$\cos 36^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}$

$\sin 18^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}$

First, substitute these values into the expression:

$\frac{3\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}+5\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}}{5\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}-3\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}}$

Simplify the numerator and the denominator:

Numerator: $3\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}+5\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}=\frac{3(\sqrt{5}+1)+5(\sqrt{5}-1)}{4}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}+3+5\sqrt{5}-5}{4}=\frac{8\sqrt{5}-2}{4}=2\sqrt{5}-\frac{1}{2}$

Denominator: $5\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}-3\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}=\frac{5(\sqrt{5}+1)-3(\sqrt{5}-1)}{4}=\frac{5\sqrt{5}+5-3\sqrt{5}+3}{4}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}+8}{4}=\frac{\sqrt{5}+4}{2}$

Now combine the simplified numerator and denominator:

$\frac{2\sqrt{5}-\frac{1}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{5}+4}{2}}=\frac{(2\sqrt{5}-\frac{1}{2})\cdot 2}{\sqrt{5}+4}=\frac{4\sqrt{5}-1}{\sqrt{5}+4}$

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying both the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$\frac{(4\sqrt{5}-1)(\sqrt{5}-4)}{(\sqrt{5}+4)(\sqrt{5}-4)}$

The denominator simplifies to:

$\sqrt{5}^{2}-4^{2}=5-16=-11$

The numerator simplifies to:

$(4\sqrt{5}-1)(\sqrt{5}-4)=(4\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{5}-4\cdot 4\sqrt{5}-1\cdot \sqrt{5}+1\cdot 4)=(20-16\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{5}+4)=24-17\sqrt{5}$

Combining them, we get:

$\frac{24-17\sqrt{5}}{-11}=\frac{17\sqrt{5}-24}{11}$

Thus, $a=17,b=24,c=11$.

Therefore, $a+b+c=17+24+11=52$.

So the correct option is:

Option B: 52
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: The number of distinct real roots of the equation $|x+1||x+3|-4|x+2|+5=0$, is $_______$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put $t=x+2$. Then $|x+1||x+3|=|t-1||t+1|=|t^{2}-1|$, and the equation becomes $|t^{2}-1|-4|t|+5=0$.

Let $u=|t|\geq 0$, so $|u^{2}-1|-4u+5=0$.

For $u\geq 1$: $u^{2}-1-4u+5=0\Rightarrow (u-2)^{2}=0\Rightarrow u=2$, which satisfies $u\geq 1$.

For $0\leq u<1$: $1-u^{2}-4u+5=0\Rightarrow u^{2}+4u-6=0\Rightarrow u=-2\pm \sqrt{10}$. Here $-2+\sqrt{10}\approx 1.16$ is not less than $1$ and $-2-\sqrt{10}<0$, so there is no root in this range.

So $|x+2|=2$, giving $x=0$ or $x=-4$; both satisfy the equation ($1\cdot 3-8+5=0$ and $3\cdot 1-8+5=0$).

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: If $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{5(x-1)^{4}(x+3)^{6}}}\mathrm{d}x=\mathrm{A}\left (\frac{αx-1}{βx+3}\right )^{B}+\mathrm{C}$, where $\mathrm{C}$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $α+β+20\mathrm{AB}$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Write the radicand in terms of $\dfrac{x-1}{x+3}$:

$(x-1)^{4}(x+3)^{6}=\left (\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right )^{4}(x+3)^{10}\Rightarrow \sqrt{5(x-1)^{4}(x+3)^{6}}=\left (\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right )^{4/5}(x+3)^{2}$

Put $t=\dfrac{x-1}{x+3}$, so $dt=\dfrac{(x+3)-(x-1)}{(x+3)^{2}}dx=\dfrac{4}{(x+3)^{2}}dx$:

$I=\int \frac{dx}{(x+3)^{2}t^{4/5}}=\frac{1}{4}\int t^{-4/5}dt=\frac{1}{4}\cdot 5t^{1/5}+C=\frac{5}{4}\left (\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right )^{1/5}+C$

Comparing with $A\left (\dfrac{αx-1}{βx+3}\right )^{B}$ gives $A=\dfrac{5}{4}$, $B=\dfrac{1}{5}$, $α=1$, $β=1$.

$α+β+20AB=1+1+20\times \frac{5}{4}\times \frac{1}{5}=7$

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}$ be the region enclosed by the parabola $y^{2}=2x$ and the line $x=24$. Then the maximum area of the rectangle inscribed in the region $\mathrm{A}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A rectangle with sides parallel to the axes is largest when one side lies on $x=24$ and the opposite side joins the points $\left (\dfrac{t^{2}}{2},\pm t\right )$ of the parabola $y^{2}=2x$, where $0<t<4\sqrt{3}$.


[IMG]

Its height is $2t$ and its width is $24-\dfrac{t^{2}}{2}$, so

$A(t)=2t\left (24-\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )=48t-t^{3}$

$A^{'}(t)=48-3t^{2}=0\Rightarrow t=4$, and $A^{''}(t)=-6t=-24<0$ at $t=4$, so the area is maximum there.

$A(4)=48\times 4-4^{3}=192-64=128$

Hence, the answer is 128.

text: Let $α|x|=|y|\mathrm{e}^{xy-β},α,β\in 𝐍$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\mathrm{d}y-y\mathrm{d}x+xy(x\mathrm{d}y+y\mathrm{d}x)=0,y(1)=2$. Then $α+β$ is equal to $________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dividing the equation by $xy$:

$\dfrac{xdy-ydx}{xy}+(xdy+ydx)=0\Rightarrow d\left (\ln \left |\dfrac{y}{x}\right |\right )+d(xy)=0.$

Integrating, $\ln \left |\dfrac{y}{x}\right |+xy=C$. From $y(1)=2$: $C=\ln 2+2$.

So $xy-2=\ln \dfrac{2|x|}{|y|}$, i.e. $e^{xy-2}=\dfrac{2|x|}{|y|}$, which gives

$2|x|=|y|e^{xy-2}.$

Comparing with $α|x|=|y|e^{xy-β}$: $α=2$ and $β=2$, so $α+β=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: If $α=\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\left (\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\tan x}}-\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x}}\right )$ and $β=\lim _{x\to 0}(1+\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2}\cot x}$ are the roots of the quadratic equation $\mathrm{a}x^{2}+\mathrm{b}x-\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}=0$, then $12\log _{\mathrm{e}}(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b})$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} α & =\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\dfrac{e^{\sqrt{\tan x}}-e^{\sqrt{x}}}{(\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x})} \\ =\lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}\left (e^{\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x}}-1\right )}{(\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x})}=1 \\ β & =\lim _{x\to 0}(1+\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2}\cot x}=\lim _{x\to 0}e^{(\sin x)\left (\frac{1}{2}\cot x\right )} \\ =\lim _{x\to 0}e^{\frac{1}{2}\cos x}=e^{1/2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Product of roots}=\sqrt{e}=\dfrac{-\sqrt{e}}{a}\Rightarrow a=-1 \\ \text{Sum of roots}=\dfrac{-b}{a}=1+\sqrt{e} \\ =b=\sqrt{e}+1 \\ \Rightarrow 12\ln (a+b)=12\ln (\sqrt{e}+1-1)=12\ln \left (e^{1/2}\right )=6 \end{array}$
